early_earth_analysis_v2/drafts/manuscrip.note: The historical vertical-axis transformation is unresolved. early_earth_analysis_v2/drafts/manuscrip.title: Angular populations around the alanine central carbon
early_earth_analysis_v2/drafts/manuscrip.description: The histogram shows two angular populations near ±125° for alanine-reference coordinates, describing substituent orientation around the central carbon.
early_earth_analysis_v2/drafts/manuscrip.note: Independent F10 reconstruction identifies the coordinate as an improper torsion and reproduces 438,986 blocks. The coordinate distribution does not assign absolute stereochemistry, equilibrium populations, or thermodynamic stability. Catalog copy from the 2026-09-27 working manuscript draft.

early_earth_analysis_v2/drafts/manuscrip.title: Alanine atoms defining the central-carbon orientation
early_earth_analysis_v2/drafts/manuscrip.description: The molecular rendering labels N, Cα, carboxyl C, and side-chain C, identifying the atom quartet used to characterize substituent orientation.
early_earth_analysis_v2/drafts/manuscrip.note: The coordinate distribution does not assign absolute stereochemistry, equilibrium populations, or thermodynamic stability. Catalog copy from the 2026-09-27 working manuscript draft.

early_earth_analysis_v2/figures/publicat.title: Reference connectivity coverage and temporal presence
early_earth_analysis_v2/figures/publicat.description: Compares observed members of a declared 457-reference library across three system sizes, then shows glycine, alanine, cytosine, thymine, and uracil match presence in 100-ps windows.
early_earth_analysis_v2/figures/publicat.note: Names mean element/connectivity compatibility with searched references. Finite-library coverage is not a complete chemical-species census.

early_earth_analysis_v2/figures/publicat.title: Starting-frame analysis time and memory
early_earth_analysis_v2/figures/publicat.description: Three fresh-process measurements per size compare end-to-end identification time and peak host memory for supplied 228- and 228,000-atom starting configurations; lines mark medians.
early_earth_analysis_v2/figures/publicat.note: Bounded same-machine starting-state benchmark, not evolved-frame workload scaling, dynamics performance, or a current speedup claim.

early_earth_analysis_v2/figures/publicat.title: String discovery in hot and quenched states
early_earth_analysis_v2/figures/publicat.description: Cumulative discovery, complete 100-ps windows, and the final hot-only/shared/quenched-only partition distinguish discoveries in the two states.
early_earth_analysis_v2/figures/publicat.note: Distinct emitted strings are representation-dependent; repeated occurrences are sampled observations, not confirmed species or yields. Quenched points are independent endpoints, and retrospective overlap differs from first-detection order.

early_earth_analysis_v2/figures/review_v.title: From reactive dynamics to connectivity comparisons
early_earth_analysis_v2/figures/review_v.description: Workflow links three simulation sizes to 3,521 saved frames per size, connectivity identification, and separate 25-fs quench branches for the Hero Run.
early_earth_analysis_v2/figures/review_v.note: Source-bound schematic; the quenches are independently initialized endpoints. Size/sampling comparisons and quench comparisons use different retained coordinate representations.

early_earth_analysis_v2/figures/review_v.title: Per-frame structural diversity across system sizes
early_earth_analysis_v2/figures/review_v.description: Bars compare mean exact-connectivity richness with abundance-weighted effective Shannon diversity for 228, 228,000, and 22.8-million-atom systems.
early_earth_analysis_v2/figures/review_v.note: All 3,521 snapshots per size receive equal weight; matched sampling does not establish identical densities or physical conditions.

early_earth_analysis_v2/figures/review_v.title: How sampling cadence changes observed variety
early_earth_analysis_v2/figures/review_v.description: Compares 1.25-ps analysis with its 2.50-ps subset, then separates additionally detected structures into those seen in one versus multiple saved frames.
early_earth_analysis_v2/figures/review_v.note: A same-source subset comparison; the independently computed sparse census is separate. One sampled occurrence does not establish a short lifetime.

early_earth_analysis_v2/figures/review_v.title: Fragment membership changes after quench
early_earth_analysis_v2/figures/review_v.description: Histograms show the fraction of atoms in changed fragments and relative component-count changes across all 3,521 paired production endpoints, with mean and median markers.
early_earth_analysis_v2/figures/review_v.note: Per-frame distributions describe cutoff connectivity changes. They do not establish reaction rates, mechanisms, or stability.

early_earth_analysis_v2/figures/sampling.title: Structural presence and first detections across size and time
early_earth_analysis_v2/figures/sampling.description: Six panels show structures present and first detected in 100-ps windows for each of the three system sizes, excluding the initial frame equally and marking the Hero Run restart.
early_earth_analysis_v2/figures/sampling.note: Each bin averages 80 analyzed frames and each panel has its own vertical scale. Archived time across the restart is not uninterrupted dynamics; no rates or extrapolations are fitted.

paper-early-earth-chemistry-hero-run/fig.title: Named-reference match occurrences before and after quench
paper-early-earth-chemistry-hero-run/fig.description: Bars compare hot and quenched component appearances for individual named references in the 250-fs quench cohort.
paper-early-earth-chemistry-hero-run/fig.note: The plotted counts are match rows, despite the historical frame-count axis label; they are not distinct-species counts or yields.

paper-early-earth-chemistry-hero-run/fig.title: Named-reference matches across simulation time
paper-early-earth-chemistry-hero-run/fig.description: Filled hot and quenched traces show named-reference match rows per simulation frame in the 250-fs quench comparison.
paper-early-earth-chemistry-hero-run/fig.note: The filled area is not a cumulative sum. The original plot compares 415 hot frames with 412 quenched endpoints; corrected paired results use 412 shared identifiers.

paper-early-earth-chemistry-hero-run/fig.title: Approximate-signature richness before and after quench
paper-early-earth-chemistry-hero-run/fig.description: Hot and quenched scatters compare the number of unique molecular signatures per frame in the 415-frame study.
paper-early-earth-chemistry-hero-run/fig.note: Approximate-signature richness differs from total fragment count and named-reference matching. This historical cohort is separate from current exact production analysis.

paper-early-earth-chemistry-hero-run/fig.title: Reference-match distributions on the higher-count scale
paper-early-earth-chemistry-hero-run/fig.description: Violin distributions compare hot and quenched named-reference match counts on the roughly 240-versus-412 scale.
paper-early-earth-chemistry-hero-run/fig.note: This belongs to a different database/code generation from the October roughly 18-versus-30 comparison. The exact March database and original plot producer remain unbound.

paper-early-earth-chemistry-hero-run/fig.title: Unique-signature counts in paired states
paper-early-earth-chemistry-hero-run/fig.description: Hot and quenched scatter traces compare unique-signature counts per frame across simulation time.
paper-early-earth-chemistry-hero-run/fig.note: Retained legacy view; signature resolution and source generations differ from later figures and the exact production census.

paper-early-earth-chemistry-hero-run/fig.title: Temperature relaxation during a quench
paper-early-earth-chemistry-hero-run/fig.description: Temperature versus integration step shows rapid cooling toward the thermostat target during the exploratory quench.
paper-early-earth-chemistry-hero-run/fig.note: Historical protocol illustration; do not use it as the timeline of the independent 25-fs production endpoints.

paper-early-earth-chemistry-hero-run/fig.title: Molecular-signature detections across time
paper-early-earth-chemistry-hero-run/fig.description: The time histogram shows signatures reported as newly synthesized along the simulation, with more detections in the early portion of the run.
paper-early-earth-chemistry-hero-run/fig.note: Historical signature-based view, with representation and wording inherited from its source. It does not establish reaction yields or rates.

paper-early-earth-chemistry-hero-run/fig.title: Reference-match distributions on the lower-count scale
paper-early-earth-chemistry-hero-run/fig.description: Hot and quenched violin plots compare named-reference match counts per frame on the roughly 18-versus-30 scale.
paper-early-earth-chemistry-hero-run/fig.note: The original distributions use 415 hot frames and 412 quenched endpoints. Corrected paired analysis uses the 412 shared identifiers; match rows are not species counts.
